findings.summary: crates/setup/src/app.rs:298: the local listener never checks the Host header, so for the 15 minutes before the App is created, a DNS-rebinding page in the owner's browser that finds the ephemeral port can read `/` (which holds the `state`), then send the browser to `/created?state=<state>&code=<code from an App manifest the attacker made under their own account>`. convert() accepts the code, and the owner is sent to install the attacker's App. match_repos's app_id check passes, because it compares against that same converted App. To fix, check that Host is `127.0.0.1:<port>` and reject anything else.

crates/setup/src/app.rs:211: convert() reads id, slug and pem but never checks the App's `owner.login` against the `gh` user the run acts as. An App converted from someone else's manifest code (see the Host finding) is treated as the board's own, installed, and its key put in sdlc-board-tokens. Checking the owner before redirecting to the install page closes this whatever way the code arrives.

crates/setup/src/app.rs:184: `/installed` needs no state, so once the App exists, any local process or web page that hits `127.0.0.1:<port>/installed?installation_id=N` ends the browser wait with N. match_repos then rejects N because its app_id doesn't match, but the owner's real install redirect is never waited for: the run installs the key and exits non-zero. Only a disruption, since nothing is installed on the wrong App. Ignoring a mismatched installation_id and waiting on would avoid it.

decision: Open the PR and advance to PR review
